title: SqueezeBench: Saturation-Resilient Evaluation of Mathematical Capability
abstract: arXiv:2610.13461v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI systems are making rapid progress in mathematics, but this progress is hard to measure. Benchmarks of solved problems saturate, and in benchmarks of open problems each problem can be resolved for the first time only once. We present SqueezeBench, a benchmark that is resilient to saturation: a success raises the bar instead of removing the problem. Each problem fixes an integer function $f(n)$ whose values are known only for small $n$, and the benchmark keeps a lower and an upper record on it. A record is a computable Lean function with a machine-checked proof that it bounds $f$. A submission proposes a new function and proves that it bounds $f$, that it is no worse than the current record at any $n$, and that it is strictly better at some $n$. Once accepted, it becomes the record that the next submission has to beat. The system thus chooses the bound as well as its proof, and it may improve the record at a single $n$ or its growth rat

translated_title: SqueezeBench：抗饱和的数学能力评估
translated_abstract: 人工智能系统在数学领域正取得快速进展，但这种进展难以衡量。针对已解决问题的基准会饱和，而在开放问题的基准中，每个问题只能被首次解决一次。我们提出了SqueezeBench，这是一个对饱和具有韧性的基准：一次成功会提高门槛，而不是移除问题。每个问题固定一个整数函数 $f(n)$，其取值仅在较小的 $n$ 时已知，该基准为它维护一个下界记录和一个上界记录。记录是一个可计算的Lean函数，并附带机器验证的证明表明它约束着 $f$。一次提交需要提出一个新函数，并证明它约束着 $f$、在任何 $n$ 处都不差于当前记录、且在某个 $n$ 处严格更优。一旦被接受，它就成为下一次提交必须超越的记录。因此，该系统既选择了界，也选择了其证明，并且可以在单个 $n$ 处改进记录，或改进其增长率……
tldr: SqueezeBench提出了一种抗饱和的数学能力评估基准，要求AI不断提出并用Lean机器验证证明整数函数的上下界记录，使每次成功都提高门槛而非消除问题。
